paragraphs.text: The leaf in this cake comes from Yiwu, in Yunnan, and dates to 2008. It had already spent time aging before it was pressed, so the cake began further along than one pressed from fresh leaf.
It is [ripe pu’er](shou:definition): the leaf was heaped warm and damp in a [fermenting pile](shou:wet-piling) before pressing, a method Yunnan’s state factories brought into production in 1973.
Eighteen years on, the leaf is well past the ten years the trade uses to mark [aged ripe pu’er](shou:age-aged). From here, storage shapes it as much as the years do.

brewing.text: From a cake, brick or tuo, ease a piece off along the edge with a pick rather than snapping it, so the leaves stay whole. Ripe pu’er takes boiling water and forgives a heavy hand. A common start is about 7 grams to 100 ml, one quick rinse, then short steeps that lengthen as the leaf opens; it gives eight or more good cups.

notice.text: A smooth, deep cup with woody, date-like or medicinal notes, which the trade calls aged aroma.
